body:
@muness is attempting to deploy a commit to the **faanng's projects** Team on [Vercel](https://vercel.com).

A member of the Team first needs to [authorize it](https://vercel.com/git/authorize?team=faanng's%20projects&slug=faanngs-projects&teamId=team_ZILZ7xU6J0psiwDMIeFOUWUL&type=github&job=%7B%22headInfo%22%3A%7B%22sha%22%3A%22f92c9e5f27edf7ea6079b9a4ba7213223d5f057d%22%7D%2C%22id%22%3A%22QmZriWUu6pCVfiRse7hZD8mc3VKzkqjv86N2YZ3zkyy2zf%22%2C%22org%22%3A%22shhivv%22%2C%22prId%22%3A3%2C%22repo%22%3A%22arc-cua%22%7D).

Repro script:

```python
"""Repro: saving an untitled TextEdit document from the background does nothing.

Run with TextEdit not frontmost:  open -g -a TextEdit && python repro_background_save.py
"""
from arc_cua import Driver
from arc_cua.backends import MacOSApp

pid = MacOSApp.from_bundle_id("com.apple.TextEdit").pid
with Driver() as driver:
    snapshot = driver.observe(pid)
    area = next(e for e in snapshot.elements if e.role == "TextArea")
    driver.act(snapshot, "TYPE_TEXT", area.id, value="background save repro")

    menu = driver.run_command(pid, "File > Save", settle=True)
    print("run_command:", menu.status, "reacted =", menu.settled and menu.settled.reacted)

    snapshot = driver.observe(pid)
    area = next(e for e in snapshot.elements if e.role == "TextArea")
    key = driver.act(snapshot, "HOTKEY", area.id, hotkey="MOD+S", settle=True)
    print("MOD+S:      ", key.status, "reacted =", key.settled and key.settled.reacted)

    sheets = [e for e in driver.observe(pid).elements if e.role in ("Sheet", "Dialog")]
    print("save sheet present:", bool(sheets))
```

Follow-up: this looks like a symptom of something broader. **After a background `TYPE_TEXT`, TextEdit's menus stay disabled for the user, even after they bring the app to the front.**

A/B on a fresh TextEdit (`open -g`, seeded document): bring it to the front, then read `enabled` of Edit > Select All through System Events, not through arc.

| Arm | Select All enabled after activation |
|---|---|
| control (no arc) | `true` (2/2) |
| arc `TYPE_TEXT` into the text area first | `false` (2/2) |

In the arc arm, the state persists after switching to another app and back, and after opening a new document. In practice, ⌘A and the Edit menu don't work in that app until it's quit. I found it because another automation tool's ⌘A was silently ignored in a TextEdit that arc had typed into, but worked in a fresh instance.

My guess, not verified: the synthetic focus/defocus records that `macos_background.borrowed_focus` posts with `SLPSPostEventRecordTo` leave AppKit's key-window bookkeeping inconsistent. That would also explain the original report here, where the menus validate as "No Document".

Repro script:

```python
"""A/B: does arc's background TYPE_TEXT leave TextEdit with its menus disabled?

For each arm: launch a fresh TextEdit in the background, make a seeded document,
optionally type into it with arc, then activate TextEdit and read whether
Edit > Select All is enabled (via System Events, not via arc).
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import time

from arc_cua import Driver
from arc_cua.backends import MacOSApp


def osa(script: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()


def fresh_textedit() -> int:
    osa('if application "TextEdit" is running then tell application "TextEdit" to quit saving no')
    time.sleep(1.5)
    subprocess.run(["open", "-g", "-a", "TextEdit"], check=True)
    time.sleep(1.5)
    osa('tell application "TextEdit" to make new document with properties {text:"seed"}')
    time.sleep(0.5)
    return MacOSApp.from_bundle_id("com.apple.TextEdit").pid


def select_all_enabled() -> str:
    osa('tell application "TextEdit" to activate')
    time.sleep(0.8)
    return osa('tell application "System Events" to tell process "TextEdit" to '
               'get enabled of menu item "Select All" of menu "Edit" of menu bar 1')


for arm in sys.argv[1:] or ["control", "arc"]:
    pid = fresh_textedit()
    if arm == "arc":
        with Driver() as driver:
            snapshot = driver.observe(pid)
            area = next(e for e in snapshot.elements if e.role == "TextArea")
            driver.act(snapshot, "TYPE_TEXT", area.id, value="typed by arc in the background")
    print(f"{arm:8} Select All enabled after activation: {select_all_enabled()}")

osa('tell application "TextEdit" to quit saving no')
```

Second app with the same failure: **Audacity 3.7.9** (wxWidgets), arc-cua 0.1.1 @ `74ffae1`, macOS 26.7.1.

Audacity was launched with `open -g` and never brought to the front. Terminal stayed frontmost the whole time.

| Step | Call | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `run_command("File > Open Recent > …/vocals.wav")` | ✅ the file opens (this command doesn't need a document) |
| 2 | `run_command("Select > All")` | ❌ `done`, but nothing is selected (the waveform and the selection readouts are unchanged) |
| 3 | `run_command("Effect > Fading > Fade Out", settle=True)` | ❌ `done`, `reacted: false`, waveform unchanged |
| 4 | `drag(pid, [[800,200],[950,200],[1100,200]])` on the waveform | ✅ selects 1:23.879–2:04.996. Accessibility then catches up all at once: toolbar buttons that had reported `enabled: false` (Zoom, Trim, Silence, Undo) now report enabled. |
| 5 | `run_command("Effect > Fading > Fade Out", settle=True)` | ✅ `reacted: true`. The fade is applied, confirmed afterwards from the exported WAV (RMS ratio 0.23 over the faded range, 1.00 elsewhere). |

As with TextEdit, `commands()` showed the document-scoped items as `enabled: false` before step 4. The new clue is that **one real input event to the window (the drag in step 4) was enough for the next document-scoped menu command to work.** That suggests the app needs to process a real event before menu validation and its key-window state are in place, and that `run_command` on a "cold" background app presses items the app still treats as disabled.

Not verified: I didn't retry `Select > All` after step 4, so I can't say whether every command recovers or only the ones that act on the selection.

This is a different symptom from the TextEdit follow-up above. There, the menus stayed disabled even after activation, once arc had typed into the app. Here they recovered after a pointer event. That may mean two separate causes, or the same one seen at different stages.

Possible mitigation: before pressing a document-scoped menu item in an app that hasn't received input from arc yet, deliver one harmless event to its window (or raise/key it through accessibility). Alternatively, report `reacted: false` from `run_command` as a distinct status, so callers don't take `done` as success.
